panels.title: API p95 latency
panels.description: Estimated percentile from histogram buckets. No observations in the recent rate window means no latency value; it does not mean zero seconds. Rates need at least two exports (60 seconds apart by default).

panels.title: Observed batch completions since process start
panels.description: Cumulative observations from currently exporting process instances, grouped by outcome. Resets on process restart; not a durable database total.

panels.title: Observed worker attempts since process start
panels.description: Cumulative observations from currently exporting process instances, grouped by outcome. Resets on process restart; not a durable database total.

panels.title: Database pool utilization

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (service_name, instance) (watermarker_db_pool_connections{state="acquired"}) / max by (service_name, instance) (watermarker_db_pool_limit)

panels.description: Acquired connections / configured limit per process. A checked-out connection can be executing SQL, waiting on a lock, or held idle. Sampled at export time; brief spikes may be missed.

panels.title: Database pool connections
panels.description: Acquired, idle and constructing connections per process. Each API, consumer and monitor instance owns its own pool; the monitor cannot inspect the API pool.

panels.title: Database pool waits and cancellations / second
panels.description: Wait counter includes only successful acquisitions that waited for a released or newly constructed connection. Canceled acquisition attempts are counted separately. Not the number currently waiting. Rates need two exports.

panels.title: Database pool mean wait for successful waiting acquires
panels.description: Mean accumulated wait time / successful waiting acquisitions. Includes connection construction waits. Canceled waits are excluded; not SQL latency or a percentile. No successful waiting acquisitions means no value.

panels.title: Database blocked and blocking sessions

targets.expr: max by (deployment_environment_name, state) (watermarker_db_lock_sessions and on (instance, source, deployment_environment_name) ((watermarker_backlog_observation_success{source="database"} == 1) and on (instance, source, deployment_environment_name) (time() - watermarker_backlog_observation_time_seconds{source="database"} < 90)))

panels.description: Client sessions waiting on Lock events and distinct positive blocker PIDs. One blocker can block multiple sessions. Sampled across the current database; excludes the monitoring query. Failed or more than 90-second-old observations are hidden, never replaced with zero. Multiple monitor replicas use max, not sum; assumes one shared database per environment.

panels.title: Database idle open transactions

targets.expr: max by (deployment_environment_name) (watermarker_db_transaction_idle and on (instance, source, deployment_environment_name) ((watermarker_backlog_observation_success{source="database"} == 1) and on (instance, source, deployment_environment_name) (time() - watermarker_backlog_observation_time_seconds{source="database"} < 90)))

panels.description: Client sessions idle inside a transaction, including aborted transactions. A pooled idle connection with no open transaction is excluded. Failed or more than 90-second-old observations are hidden, never replaced with zero. Multiple monitor replicas use max, not sum; assumes one shared database per environment.

panels.title: Database oldest open transaction

targets.expr: max by (deployment_environment_name) (watermarker_db_transaction_oldest_age_seconds and on (instance, source, deployment_environment_name) ((watermarker_backlog_observation_success{source="database"} == 1) and on (instance, source, deployment_environment_name) (time() - watermarker_backlog_observation_time_seconds{source="database"} < 90)))

panels.description: Age of the oldest open client transaction, including active and idle transactions. Not a completed-transaction percentile or proof that this transaction is blocking anyone. Failed or more than 90-second-old observations are hidden, never replaced with zero. Multiple monitor replicas use max, not sum; assumes one shared database per environment.
